sentences.text: Pagosvenator shares specific traits with other erpetosuchids, such as maxillary teeth restricted to the front of the mouth and a maxilla portion under the lacrimal that is higher than long.
The fossils, which include a skull, some vertebrae, and osteoderms, were anonymously donated to the Candelária Museum in 2015.
The type species Pagosvenator candelariensis was formally described in 2018.
Before its formal description in 2018, Pagosvenator was allied with the ornithosuchids, but its parent group is the family Erpetosuchidae.

Pagosvenator lived during the Mid-Late Triassic in the Dinodontosaurus Assemblage Zone of the Santa Maria Supergroup in Brazil, specifically from the Ladinian to the Carnian stages between 241.464 and 227.3 million years ago.
